dialogue.chat.jaymoskingdoms.keeper_tale: Our city in the sands didn't fall in a day. It fell in the old age, when the Warrior-born raiders and the orcs came over the world. The long defence turned them back, but too late for us.
The Sun-Crowned Dead lies under the steps, with the guard who stood with them to the end. We stay so that sleep isn't broken. Leave the tomb shut, stranger. I know most don't.
You wonder why we ask for emeralds? The green stone was our people's money. The realms' coin never was.
The map on my stall follows the old road our people traded along, to the nearest city of another people. Walk it and you walk where they walked.
The stepped tombs were the Lantern Warden's. His light was kept over our rulers so the dark couldn't have them, and we keep his fire lit still.
Bring the Warden a lantern, a candle, a bone. Light given back to the one who keeps the dark off. The walking dead are his to put down, and the blood-drinkers hate his light.
Our city on the plains didn't fall in a day. It fell in the old age, when the Warrior-born raiders and the orcs came over the world. The long defence turned them back, but too late for us.
Our consuls were chosen, not born. The Last Consul was chosen in the year the raiders came, and never laid the office down. He lies under the hall now.
You wonder why we ask for emeralds? The green stone was our people's money. The realms' coin never was.
The map on my stall follows the old road our people traded along, to the nearest city of another people. Walk it and you walk where they walked.
The Hearthkeeper's temple stood open on every side, so no traveller was ever turned away. That is why we still sell to anyone who comes.
The legionaries went down into the tomb with the Last Consul of their own will. We keep the Hearthkeeper's fire lit over them. Leave them their sleep, if you can.
Our halls in the north didn't fall in a day. It fell in the old age, when the Warrior-born raiders and the orcs came over the world. The long defence turned them back, but too late for us.
The Barrow-King lies in the mound with his hearth-guard, who stood with him to the end. We stay so that sleep isn't broken. Leave the barrow shut, stranger. I know most don't.
You wonder why we ask for emeralds? The green stone was our people's money. The realms' coin never was.
The map on my stall follows the old road our people traded along, to the nearest city of another people. Walk it and you walk where they walked.
The long halls and the mounds were the Crowned Sun's. Our kings were crowned there and laid down there. Don't mistake them for the moor's barrows. Those keep the Lantern Warden's light.
The Crowned Sun takes tribute as a king does: gold in small coin, the sunflower, glowstone. He is warm to those who serve a crown. Thieves are his shame.
Our court in Blossom didn't fall in a day. It fell in the old age, when the Warrior-born raiders and the orcs came over the world. The long defence turned them back, but too late for us.
The Jade Empress lies under the palace with her sworn blades, who stood with her to the end. We stay so that sleep isn't broken. Leave her tomb shut, stranger. I know most don't.
You wonder why we ask for emeralds? The green stone was our people's money. The realms' coin never was.
The map on my stall follows the old road our people traded along, to the nearest city of another people. Walk it and you walk where they walked.
The palace was the Ash Whisperer's: all hidden rooms and doors that open the wrong way. She loved quick hands and a shut mouth. So did the court.
Bring the Whisperer coal, charcoal, black powder, a squid's ink. Things that burn or hide. The Sun's men hang her followers when they catch them, so her faithful keep quiet.
Our halls in the mountain didn't fall in a day. It fell in the old age, when the Warrior-born raiders and the orcs came over the world. The long defence turned them back, but too late for us.
Our last ruler lies under the hall with the guard who stood with them to the end. We stay so that sleep isn't broken. Leave the tomb shut, stranger. I know most don't.

Our halls were the Anvil-Father's, cut down into the mines where the first seams were opened. He loves a true blow and a deep cut into the mountain.
Bring the Anvil-Father iron, copper or gold, raw from the seam or poured. And keep his work from the sea. She rusts whatever he makes.

The Deep Mother's temples stand on the sea floor among the drowned colonnades. We keep their sea-stone lamps lit still.
Give the Deep Mother a little of what she gives: fish, shell, whale bone, a pearl of ambergris. Her children hunt the great whales. She doesn't forgive the miners' god.
Our home in the deep woods didn't fall in a day. It fell in the old age, when the Warrior-born raiders and the orcs came over the world. The long defence turned them back, but too late for us.

The shrine was the Green Huntsman's: a ring of stones round antler and bone. He walks without a sound and knows where the old beasts lie.
Leave the Huntsman hide and feather, a hare's foot, good red meat, where he can find it. Dress what you kill and waste none. That was our only law of the hunt.
Our house didn't fall in a day. It fell in the old age, when the Warrior-born raiders and the orcs came over the world. The long defence turned them back, but too late for us.

Our people held the Truth above the rest. It kept no temple on the ground. Its old house is in the Aether, among the sky's remnants, bare of any idol.
Those who keep to the Truth still go up to its house. Make an offering there and its champion comes down, as at every old temple.
dialogue.chat.jaymoskingdoms.keeper_wait: That's all I'll tell today. Come back and trade, and there's more.
Trade with me again, and I'll tell you more of the city.
The rest keeps. Come back when you've business at my stall.
dialogue.chat.jaymoskingdoms.keeper_done: You've heard all I know of our city. Keep it better than the raiders did.
I've told you everything my mother told me. Pass it on.
There's no more to tell. Only what's down there, and that should stay shut.
dialogue.chat.jaymoskingdoms.keeper_word: They look you over and say something in the old tongue. You don't follow.
